vocabulary.meaning_en: be able to come or attend
vocabulary.note_ar: I can't make it = لا أستطيع الحضور
vocabulary.note_en: I can't make it = I can't come.
vocabulary.example: Sorry, I can't make it to lunch on Wednesday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: happen suddenly, usually a problem or something urgent
vocabulary.example: Something urgent has come up at work.
I'm tied up in meetings all afternoon.

vocabulary.meaning_en: one right after the other, with no break
vocabulary.example: I have meetings back to back today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: move an event to an earlier time
vocabulary.example: Can we bring the meeting forward to 12 o'clock?

vocabulary.meaning_en: move an event to a later time
vocabulary.note_ar: ويقال أيضًا push out أو put back
vocabulary.example: Let's push the meeting back to 4 o'clock.
They called off the match because of the rain.

vocabulary.meaning_en: move an event to a later date
vocabulary.example: We had to postpone the trip until next month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: give an event a new time or date
vocabulary.example: We'll reschedule the meeting for Thursday.

vocabulary.note_en: That's a pity = that's a shame.
vocabulary.example: You can't come? That's a pity.

vocabulary.meaning_en: feel happy about something that will happen
vocabulary.note_ar: بعدها اسم أو فعل بـ ing
vocabulary.example: I was looking forward to meeting you.
What do you reckon? Should I take the job?
Let me clarify what I mean.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the way you see or understand something
vocabulary.example: We have different perceptions of the problem.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an agreement where each side accepts less than it wanted
vocabulary.example: After a long talk, we reached a compromise.

vocabulary.meaning_en: please be patient with me for a short time
vocabulary.example: Bear with me while I find the file.

vocabulary.meaning_en: take a moment to think and get ready
vocabulary.example: Give me a moment to gather my thoughts.
I know what you're going through.

fine_lines.title: bring forward vs push back
fine_lines.explanation_ar: bring forward = تقديم الموعد إلى وقت أبكر (من 2 إلى 12). push back أو push out = تأخير الموعد إلى وقت لاحق (من 2 إلى 4).
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Bring forward" = make it earlier (2pm → 12pm). "Push back" / "push out" = make it later (2pm → 4pm).

examples.sentence: Can we bring the meeting forward to 11?
Can we push the meeting back to 5?

fine_lines.title: call off vs postpone
fine_lines.explanation_ar: call off = إلغاء الحدث نهائيًا. postpone = تأجيله إلى وقت لاحق.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Call off" = cancel. "Postpone" = move to a later time.

examples.sentence: We called off the trip. We're not going.
We postponed the trip until June.

expressions.phrase: I'm afraid I can't make it.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to say you cannot come.
expressions.example: I'm afraid I can't make it on Wednesday. Can we meet next week?

expressions.meaning_en: Says something unexpected stops you; you don't need to explain.
expressions.example: Sorry, something has come up. I need to change our plans.

expressions.meaning_ar: أنا مشغول طوال فترة بعد الظهر.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you are too busy to meet.
expressions.example: I'm tied up all afternoon. How about tomorrow?

expressions.phrase: Can we bring the meeting forward?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks to have the meeting earlier.
expressions.example: Can we bring the meeting forward to 11 o'clock?

expressions.phrase: Can we push the meeting back / out?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks to have the meeting later.
expressions.example: Can we push the meeting back to 4?

expressions.phrase: I have to call off the meeting.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you must cancel the meeting.
expressions.example: I'm out of town tomorrow, so I have to call off the meeting.

expressions.phrase: Can we do it on Tuesday instead?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكننا القيام به يوم الثلاثاء بدلًا من ذلك؟
expressions.meaning_en: Suggests a new day.
expressions.example: I can't make it tomorrow. Can we do it on Tuesday instead?

expressions.phrase: Oh, that's a pity. I was looking forward to it.
expressions.meaning_en: A kind reply when someone cancels.
expressions.example: Oh, that's a pity. I was looking forward to meeting you.

expressions.meaning_en: Tells someone not to feel bad.
expressions.example: Don't worry about it. Just tell me when you're free.

expressions.meaning_en: An informal way to say "it's OK".
expressions.example: No worries. These things happen.

expressions.meaning_en: Says the change is fine.
expressions.example: No problem. Tell me when you're available.

expressions.meaning_en: Says problems are normal and not anyone's fault.
expressions.example: Don't feel bad. Things happen.

expressions.meaning_ar: ما رأيك في ...؟ / ما شعورك تجاه ...؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asks for someone's opinion of an idea.
expressions.example: How do you feel about going away for the weekend?

expressions.meaning_en: Asks for someone's opinion.
expressions.example: What do you think of painting the kitchen?

expressions.meaning_en: A very informal way to ask for an opinion.
expressions.example: Should I buy a new car now? What do you reckon?

expressions.meaning_en: Explains your idea more clearly.
expressions.example: What I mean is, you need to be very precise.

expressions.meaning_en: Gives the reason for a decision or change.
expressions.example: The reason for this is that the manager is away.

expressions.meaning_en: Points to the most important problem.
expressions.example: The main problem is that we don't have enough time.

expressions.meaning_en: Asks for a chance to explain.
expressions.example: Just let me explain what we're trying to do.

expressions.meaning_en: An informal way to start an explanation, often a problem.
expressions.example: Well, the thing is, I'm really busy that day.

expressions.phrase: I have something important I'd like to discuss with you.
expressions.meaning_ar: لديّ أمر مهم أودّ مناقشته معك.
expressions.meaning_en: Warns someone that a serious talk is coming.
expressions.example: Do you have a minute? I have something important I'd like to discuss with you.

expressions.phrase: I'd like to talk to you about ...
expressions.meaning_en: Introduces a serious topic.
expressions.example: I'd like to talk to you about your exam results.

expressions.phrase: I need your help with something.
expressions.meaning_ar: أحتاج إلى مساعدتك في أمر ما.
expressions.meaning_en: Asks for help.
expressions.example: I need your help with this report. I can't do it on my own.

expressions.phrase: I think we have different perceptions about this.
expressions.meaning_ar: أظن أن لدينا تصوّرات مختلفة حول هذا.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to say you see things very differently.
expressions.example: I think we have different perceptions about this project.

expressions.phrase: I'd like to see if we could reach a better understanding.
expressions.meaning_ar: أودّ أن نرى إن كان بإمكاننا الوصول إلى تفاهم أفضل.
expressions.meaning_en: A formal way to suggest finding a compromise.
expressions.example: I'd like to see if we could reach a better understanding about the budget.

expressions.meaning_en: Says you feel worried about something coming.
expressions.example: I'm really nervous about the job interview.

expressions.meaning_en: Asks for a short time to get ready.
expressions.example: Just give me a moment to gather my thoughts.

expressions.meaning_en: Asks people to be patient.
expressions.example: Bear with me for a few minutes. Let me finish, then you can ask questions.

expressions.phrase: This keeps me up at night.
expressions.meaning_ar: هذا يجعلني أسهر طوال الليل (من القلق).
expressions.meaning_en: Says something worries you so much you can't sleep.
expressions.example: The exam keeps me up at night.

expressions.phrase: I just can't stop thinking about it.
expressions.meaning_ar: لا أستطيع التوقف عن التفكير فيه.
expressions.meaning_en: Says something is always on your mind.
expressions.example: I just can't stop thinking about the interview.

expressions.meaning_en: Offers help to someone with a problem.
expressions.example: You look worried. How can I help?

expressions.phrase: I know exactly what you're going through.
expressions.meaning_en: Shows you understand because you had the same problem.
expressions.example: I know exactly what you're going through. I've been there myself.

expressions.meaning_en: Very informal (slang): says something is very bad. Use only with close friends.
expressions.example: You lost your phone? That really sucks.

grammar.title: look forward to + -ing
grammar.explanation_ar: to في look forward to حرف جر، لذلك يأتي بعدها اسم أو فعل بـ ing وليس المصدر.
grammar.explanation_en: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so use a noun or -ing after it, not the base verb.
examples: I was looking forward to meeting you.
We're looking forward to the holiday.
I look forward to hearing from you.

grammar.title: How do you feel about / What do you think of + -ing
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد about وof (حروف جر) نستخدم الفعل بـ ing أو اسمًا.
grammar.explanation_en: After the prepositions "about" and "of", use -ing or a noun.
examples: How do you feel about going away this weekend?
What do you think of painting the bedroom?
What do you think of the new plan?

grammar.title: Separable phrasal verbs: bring it forward, push it back, call it off
grammar.explanation_ar: يمكن وضع المفعول به بعد الفعل الاصطلاحي أو في وسطه. إذا كان المفعول ضميرًا (it/them) فيجب وضعه في الوسط.
grammar.explanation_en: The object can go after the phrasal verb or in the middle. If the object is a pronoun (it/them), it must go in the middle.
examples: Can we bring the meeting forward? / Can we bring it forward?
Let's push the meeting back. / Let's push it back.
They called off the game. / They called it off.

questions.question: Your meeting is at 2pm. You want it at 12pm. You say:
A friend cancels lunch. Which reply is kind?
questions.explanation_ar: No worries. These things happen رد لطيف على الإلغاء.
questions.explanation_en: "No worries. These things happen" is a kind reply.

questions.question: I was looking forward to ___ you.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد look forward to نستخدم الفعل بـ ing.

questions.question: People keep asking questions in your presentation. You say:
choices: Bear with me. Let me finish first.
questions.explanation_ar: Bear with me تطلب من الناس الصبر قليلًا.
questions.explanation_en: "Bear with me" asks people to be patient.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: الضمير it يوضع في وسط الفعل الاصطلاحي.
questions.explanation_en: The pronoun "it" goes in the middle of the phrasal verb.

questions.question: "I know exactly what you're going through" shows:
Which is the most FORMAL?
choices: I'd like to see if we could reach a better understanding.
questions.explanation_ar: هذه العبارة رسمية، أما الأخرى فغير رسمية.
questions.explanation_en: This one is formal; the others are informal.
